prompt.context: Your client is faced with dramatic changes in the industry. As it adjusts its strategy, reacts to changes and anticipates future changes, it is concerned about its ability to keep its employees prepared for the challenges they will face. The client is also concerned about its traditional approach to learning and development and has questions about the return on investment of its programs. Your team was retained to help assess the effectiveness of the organization's learning center, develop a go forward learning strategy, and to select and implement an 'appropriate' enterprise learning management system (LMS) solution that will allow the client's learning center to successfully execute its learning strategy while simplifying its operational processes and allowing it to scale for future growth.
prompt.question: What approach would you take to assessing the client's current learning capabilities and developing the go forward strategy? What issues would you consider regarding the selection and implementation of the Learning Management System?

framework: Review current learning activities: balance of instructor-led training, e-Learning, and other learning methods
Assess degree of learning evaluation used (Reaction, Learning, Transfer, Results — Kirkpatrick levels)
Meet with leadership to determine requirements of the new strategy
Assess ability of existing programs to address identified needs; identify needs for additional learning programs
Address LMS selection and implementation: integration, data migration, self-service, access, scalability, performance

questions.prompt: How would you assess the client's current learning capabilities?
questions.guidance: Candidate should cover: (1) reviewing current learning methods mix (instructor-led vs. e-learning vs. other); (2) assessing the degree of evaluation/measurement of learning effectiveness across Kirkpatrick's four levels — Reaction, Learning, Transfer, Results; (3) reviewing individual learning plans; (4) conducting a skill gap analysis; (5) assessing whether existing programs can address identified gaps and where new programs are needed.

questions.prompt: What factors would you consider for selecting and implementing an enterprise Learning Management System (LMS)?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: integration with the existing HRIS system; data migration, system configuration, and interface development; self-service registration capabilities for employees; degree of network vs. remote access needed; scalability to support future growth; and performance of the system.

recommendation: Conduct a thorough current-state assessment of learning activities and evaluation practices before selecting a new system
Align the go-forward learning strategy with leadership-defined business requirements and skill gap analysis findings
Select an LMS that integrates with the HRIS, supports self-service registration, offers remote access, and is scalable
risks: Selecting an LMS before the learning strategy is finalized may lead to misalignment
Insufficient change management may limit adoption of new learning methods and the new system
Skill gap analysis may reveal training needs that require significant investment or curriculum development
next_steps: Facilitate workshops with leadership to define go-forward learning strategy requirements
Complete full skill gap analysis and map existing programs to identified gaps
Issue RFP for LMS vendors and evaluate against defined criteria (integration, scalability, access, performance)
